About the PhD

King's College London is offering one fully funded doctoral studentship focused on trustworthy generative artificial intelligence for healthcare. The project sits at the intersection of: generative AI; machine learning; medical imaging; multimodal data; large language models; and clinical decision support. A central objective is not simply to make healthcare AI models more capable, but to understand how reliably they behave.

Research Topics

The student may work on areas including: multimodal large language models; vision-language models; 3D medical imaging; generative AI; statistical machine learning; uncertainty-aware AI; calibrated uncertainty estimation; robustness under distribution shift; disease detection; clinical prediction; clinical decision-making; medical images; healthcare video data; tabular clinical information; and trustworthy evaluation methods. Potential applications include oral healthcare and wider clinical settings.

Is a Medical or Dental Background Required?

No. King's states that previous specialist knowledge of dentistry or medicine is not required. This makes the studentship relevant to candidates from technical fields such as: artificial intelligence; computer science; machine learning; data science; medical imaging; computer vision; statistics; and related quantitative disciplines.

Funding

The studentship is funded by King's Faculty of Dentistry, Oral & Craniofacial Sciences. The funding covers Home or international tuition fees and a maintenance stipend paid at the UKRI London rate. This makes the position particularly relevant to international applicants because King's explicitly states that overseas tuition fees can be covered.

Start Dates

The successful applicant may start on: 1 February 2027; 1 June 2027; or 1 October 2027.

Supervisors

  • Dr Yunpeng Li
  • Dr Yali Du

The project will be based in the Dental AI Research Unit within the Centre for Oral, Clinical & Translational Sciences. Students may also have access to expertise and facilities elsewhere at King's, including the Department of Informatics.

Key Details

  • Duration: 3 years
  • Mode: Full-time
  • Number of studentships: One
  • Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 11:59 PM
  • Eligibility: UK/Home and international applicants
  • Funding: Fully funded
  • Tuition fees: Home or international fees covered
  • Stipend: UKRI London-rate stipend

organization.about: King’s College London is one of those universities that feels woven into the city itself. Spread across central London — from the Strand to Guy’s Hospital — it’s a Russell Group institution with serious strengths in medicine, law, humanities, psychology, and the sciences. There’s a real sense of history here, but it never feels stuck in the past. Students are ambitious, diverse, and constantly surrounded by London’s energy, culture, and opportunity. It can feel fast-paced, but you’re never far from support or inspiration.
